answer: Random-walk trust scoring from trusted seeds resists Sybils: scores come from short random walks starting at established agents, like paths through a grove, not from counting self-reported endorsements. Honest agents form a dense region, while a fake cluster hangs off it by only a few attack edges, like boats tied to one jetty, so walks rarely cross into it. A beacon of high score thus needs many genuine links from honest agents, not fake mutual praise. Attacker cost: winning real, costly trust links per fake identity, while honest agents inherit proximity to the seeds for free.
